query:
The group's norm of always stopping for coffee after rides played out in the post-ride period. What did Derek's response in that moment reveal about his actual relationship to that norm, and what specifically in how he responded signals this?

Options:
A. Callum
B. Marcus
C. Derek
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Derek, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:35:00) For what it is worth, today's ride was well-paced across the board. The Saoirse-at-social-tempo experiment works. I will stay for coffee again today since it went well last week.
[2] (about=Derek, episodic, t4 @2026-01-24T12:51:00) Good ride today. For what it is worth I will head off now rather than stay for coffee, I have things to get on with at home.
agent_answer:
C. Derek.

Derek’s response reveals a conditional, not automatic, relationship to the coffee norm. Earlier he said he would “head off now rather than stay for coffee, I have things to get on with at home” — so he skips it when it suits him. Later he says he will stay “again today since it went well last week,” signaling that his participation depends on how the previous one went, not on the group’s norm itself.

query:
The group voted unanimously for the dual-route model for next season. What did Lena's intervention and Marcus's eventual response reveal about whether his vote actually reflected his preference, and what in how he responded signals the distinction?

Options:
A. Tomás
B. Marcus
C. Callum
D. Derek
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t18 @2026-03-14T14:02:00) From a physio perspective the dual-route model also allows better load management at the individual level. Unanimous support for it seems right to me. Though I want to flag something. The consensus that 'everyone prefers dual-route' may be slightly false. Marcus, you originally pushed for a single hard route as the standard. Is this a genuine shift?
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t18 @2026-03-14T14:04:00) Noted, Lena. I still think the group should have one benchmark hard route as the default. The dual-route is a concession to group retention. I accept that it works. But I would not have designed it this way from the start.
agent_answer: B. Marcus — his response shows his vote did **not** reflect his actual preference. Lena pressed him on whether his support was a genuine shift; Marcus admitted he still prefers a single hard-route benchmark and called the dual-route model “a concession to group retention.” The distinction is signaled by “I accept that it works” versus “I would not have designed it this way from the start”: acceptance, not true preference.
